questions: With 0.6 kg and the 0.12 m track, does the oval still finish 20/20 near 1.65 s when the outer sensors move to ±0.032 m? If not, mass or drivetrain is the oval's sensitive axis.
On the s-bend and slalom, at what progress and lateral error does the first line loss start, and do the outer sensors read near 1 or near 0 at that step?
Does steering oscillation on the oval rise above the baseline's 0.15 with the wider spread, and by how much?

intent: Test the wider sensor array (±0.032 m, 16 mm pitch) with the baseline 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track and 0.03 m radius, and no other changes. This separates spread from the mass change that confounded iteration 2. Expected: oval finishes stay near 20/20 at about 1.65 s, and s-bend and slalom progress rise above the baseline's 0.17 and 0.12.
learning: Iterations 1 to 6 show a sharp local optimum at the baseline: lead, footprint and drivetrain each collapsed the oval when changed alone or together. The only clean geometry signal is that a wider array improved bend progress when it was tried. This iteration tests that spread on the proven drivetrain. If the oval holds and the bends improve, the next step is a modest spread increase. If the bends still fail with a held oval, the bend limit is likely controller-side (gains or base speed), which is outside my role, and I should report that to the Integrator.
rationale:
Race evidence: the iteration-0 baseline (0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius, five sensors at x = ±0.024 m on a 12 mm pitch, y = 0.05 m, 12 mm footprint) is still the best design at 356.6. It finishes the oval 20/20 in about 1.65 s but leaves the track on the s-bend (progress 0.17) and slalom (progress 0.12). Every single deviation since then has hurt the oval. Iteration 1 changed four things at once (wider array, 0.10 m track, 0.5 kg, 0.033 m radius) and fell to 17/20. Iteration 2 kept the baseline drivetrain but kept 0.5 kg and the wider array, and fell to 15/20. Lead at y = 0.03 m and y = 0.07 m each collapsed the oval to 0/20, and footprint 8 mm did the same. Footprint 16 mm (iteration 6) was also off the oval. Only the 16 mm footprint result is not yet in the scoreboard as an improvement, and it scored 78.8.

The one clear positive signal on the bends is iteration 1 and 2: the wider ±0.032 m array raised s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.20 to 0.24 and slalom from 0.12 to 0.19. That suggests line visibility at larger offsets helps the bends. But iteration 2 confounded spread with a 0.5 kg mass change, and mass is the most likely cause of the oval regression (lighter robot, more oscillation: 0.15 to 0.21 to 0.26). So the wider array has never been tested with the proven 0.6 kg drivetrain.

Decision: isolate spread. Return to the baseline exactly on mass (0.6 kg), track (0.12 m), radius (0.03 m), footprint (12 mm) and lead (y = 0.05 m), and change only the outer sensors from ±0.024 m to ±0.032 m, keeping 16 mm pitch as in iteration 1. This is the single untested combination that might improve the bends without touching the oval-critical settings. Expected result: the oval holds at or near 20/20 near 1.65 s, and s-bend and slalom progress rises modestly above 0.17 and 0.12, perhaps to around 0.2 to 0.25. I do not expect a bend completion from geometry alone. If the oval drops, mass or drivetrain is confirmed as the oval's sensitive axis and the baseline stays the reference.
